anatomy.title: Anatomy of a Prosecution
anatomy.subtitle: The same transaction has been confirmed by a court as lawful — and declared a crime.
anatomy.text: We pass no verdict and seek no acquittal. We ask one thing: that all available evidence be examined. This site breaks the case down layer by layer — from commercial contracts to international procedures. The documents speak for themselves. Readers will draw their own conclusions.

legal.title: ⚖️ Legal Dissonance
legal.text: Arbitration courts up to the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation confirmed: the transaction is lawful. The criminal prosecution qualifies the same transaction as fraud. The investigation's own records document the phrase 'the value must be real' — and treat it as evidence of a conspiracy to understate value. A state that inverts the meaning of its own documents does not merely harm one individual — it undermines the very foundation of the rule of law.
legal.question: Can demanding a fair market value be evidence of a conspiracy to understate it?

international.title: 🌍 International Perimeter
international.text: The case has moved beyond a bilateral dispute. Serbia, Interpol, the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention, the ECHR — each of these institutions exists precisely to verify whether the rule of law is being upheld where national mechanisms fail. This is not pressure on a court. This is exactly what international law was created for.

sidebar.title: Media Archive
sidebar.manifesto: The media archive is not a news digest — it is an external audit of the case. Each publication here represents an independent record of facts acknowledged by the professional journalistic community: the contradictions in the Lagovsky case exist, and they are documented.

news.title: Serbian court refused to examine defence evidence — only formal documentation from Moscow
news.desc: The Court of Appeal stated plainly that it was concerned only with the document received, not with the substance of the charges. The transaction at the heart of the case has been recognised as lawful by arbitration courts up to the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation — these rulings were not taken into account.
news.focus: The defence lawyer documented violations: insufficient evidence for a reasonable suspicion — a basic prerequisite for extradition — as well as the requesting party's withdrawal from the UN Convention Against Torture and the Council of Europe. N1 is a CNN-affiliated channel; the publication means violations have been recorded by an independent source.

news.title: Serbia one step from extradition: case passes to the Minister of Justice
news.desc: The Belgrade Court of Appeal confirmed the conditions for extradition on 3 December. The final decision has been referred to the Minister of Justice — the last instance against whose decision no legal remedy exists.
news.focus: Defence lawyer Marko Štambuk notes that in practice ministers of justice very rarely refuse extradition once courts have established formal grounds. Publication in a European media network means the case has moved beyond the Serbian legal space.

news.title: Interpol CCF confirmed: complaint accepted, Red Notice under review
news.desc: The Interpol Commission for the Control of Files (CCF) notified the defence that the complaint against the Red Notice has been accepted for review (ref. CCF/135/R1610.25). Russia issued the notice on 25 January 2025, based on a warrant issued in absentia on 27 December 2024.
news.focus: The defence challenges the Red Notice under Article 3 of the Interpol Constitution: the dispute is commercial in nature and the transaction has been recognised as lawful by arbitration courts up to the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation. The CCF granted one month for submission of additional materials.
